headline: Guardrails Before Gains
thesis: As half of K-12 schools report a cyber incident and only about 3 in 10 have a formal AI policy, schools and colleges are writing the rules for AI while the tools keep arriving.
summary: Monday's digest opens on governance gaps. A Center for Internet Security report, covered by EdTech Magazine, found that half of K-12 schools had a cybersecurity incident last year and that just over 3 in 10 have put a formal AI policy in place. The fight over Google's plan to switch AI and Search off by default for student accounts continues, with districts testing filters and plug-ins that hide AI Overviews. In higher ed, Inside Higher Ed reports that hidden 'write a positive review' prompts have turned up in published journal papers. Two political stories also landed today: Rep. Virginia Foxx, a member of the House Education and Workforce Committee since 2005, lost her seat, and Florida advanced a rule that would require private colleges to answer the Education Department's 'Call to Action' or lose state licensure. On standards, 1EdTech's 2027 Learning Impact Award nominations close tonight at 11:59 p.m. ET, and Ed-Fi's API v8.1 rollout continues.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 23, 2026 · Items were gathered through web search rather than direct page fetches. Several sources published nothing new over the weekend and show their most recent items.
